issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect PersonService.getAllPersons(...) to accept a PersonSortingOptions parameter (Part 3). The template declares getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) but the solution's PersonService implements getAllPersons() without any parameter, while the solution's PersonResource still calls personService.getAllPersons(new PersonSortingOptions(...)). This mismatch is a structural inconsistency that would cause compilation errors and confuse students about the intended API surface.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the service API consistent: restore or add the parameter to the solution's PersonService by changing the signature to getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) and implement the sorting logic. Alternatively, modify PersonResource to call a no-arg getAllPersons() if sorting is intentionally moved elsewhere — but the former keeps the design consistent with the problem statement and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect PersonService.getAllPersons to accept a PersonSortingOptions parameter (to perform server-side sorting). The solution, however, contains a PersonService.getAllPersons() method with no parameter while PersonResource in the solution calls personService.getAllPersons(new PersonSortingOptions(...)). This mismatch (presence vs. absence of the sortingOptions parameter) creates a conceptual and compilation inconsistency: students are instructed to pass sorting options to the service, the resource forwards them, but the service signature in the solution does not accept them.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the PersonService API consistent: implement getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) in PersonService (and perform the requested sorting), so PersonResource can call personService.getAllPersons(new PersonSortingOptions(...)) without signature mismatch. Alternatively, if intended, change PersonResource to call a no-arg getAllPersons(), but aligning to the problem statement (service accepting PersonSortingOptions) is recommended.
